name: Neeru Fireblade
summary: In Orgrimmar, Neeru Fireblade studies dark arts he says can protect the Horde. Margoz sends you from Durotar with a Searing Collar taken from the Burning Blade cult, hoping the warlock can explain its demonic power.

sections.title: A Shaman's Limits
sections.body: Margoz has found the limit of shamanic arts. The collars taken from Burning Blade cultists at Skull Rock carry demonic sorcery, beyond what he can unravel. Shamans draw on the elements and ancestral spirits, so Margoz sends you to a warlock in the capital to learn what the collars do.

sections.title: Into the Cleft of Shadow
sections.body: Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow lies beneath its red cliffs. Warlocks and other practitioners of forbidden magic work there under Thrall's wary eye. Neeru Fireblade lives in the cavern and says he studies fel power to thwart demonic threats. When you bring him the collar, his curiosity turns Durotar's investigation toward the warlock enclave.

faq.q: Why does Margoz send me to a warlock?
faq.answer: Margoz is a shaman, drawing power from the elements and ancestral spirits. The Searing Collars from Skull Rock are demonic, so he needs someone trained in fel magic and the dark arts to understand their enchantments and origins.

faq.q: Where can I find Neeru Fireblade?
faq.answer: You can find Neeru Fireblade in the Cleft of Shadow beneath Orgrimmar, where warlocks, rogues, and shadow casters gather.

Margoz doubts Neeru's claims that his occult research is benign and meant to fight demons. Thrall permits warlocks in Orgrimmar under strict supervision, but whether Neeru can be trusted remains uncertain.
The Example Collar is one of the Searing Collars taken from Burning Blade cultists at Skull Rock. Margoz gives it to you to bring to Neeru Fireblade for magical study.

faq.q: What happens after giving the collar to Neeru?
faq.answer: Neeru examines the collar closely and sends you deeper into the investigation of the cult's presence in Durotar, beginning the search for Ak'Zeloth.

faq.q: Why does the Horde allow warlocks in Orgrimmar?
faq.answer: Thrall allows warlocks in Orgrimmar out of pragmatic necessity. He keeps them in the Cleft of Shadow, where their dangerous research can be watched, controlled, and sometimes used to understand demonic enemies.

angles.text: As a shaman, you know the elements will not commune with fel artifacts. Margoz has reached the boundary of his craft and needs a warlock's help.
As a warlock, you meet Neeru Fireblade in the Cleft of Shadow, Orgrimmar's most prominent warlock. Your forbidden craft has practical use to the Horde.
As a member of the Horde, you see a fragile truce in Orgrimmar: the Warchief's shamans sometimes rely on the shadowy outcasts of the Cleft of Shadow to protect Durotar.
